prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1017; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road and said the other vehicle drifted into their lane as they were merging. They stated they were taken to hospital by ambulance with a head injury and were diagnosed with a concussion.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the photos taken at the scene. The damage pattern along the driver's side is consistent with the described impact, and the other driver's statement matches the claimant's account in its main points.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant by phone to confirm the sequence of events. They gave the same account as in the first report and described the impact as a sharp jolt from the right that threw them against the side of the cabin.

Entry 4: Obtained statements from two independent witnesses who saw the vehicles make contact as one was changing lanes. Both described the same sequence and neither had any connection to the parties involved.

Entry 5: Checked the claimant's medical records supplied with the claim. Treatment included imaging, a period of rest, and follow-up appointments, and the notes show symptoms easing steadily over several weeks. No earlier injury to the same area appears in the records we hold.

Entry 6: Confirmed with the claimant that the driver is named on the policy and that the vehicle was insured under this policy at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the start of coverage, and no prior damage to the vehicle is recorded.

Entry 7: Noted that the claimant was not certain which seat position they occupied at the moment of impact, and recalled being unsure whether they had been seated toward the centre or the passenger side. This has been recorded as stated and does not change the consistency of the rest of the account.

Entry 8: Repair estimate has been received and its line items align with the damage seen in the photos and the reported impact. Medical and vehicle findings are being progressed for settlement review, and the claim is recommended to proceed on the current evidence.
